name: Question 9
problem:
Consider the set $B=(-\infty ,\pi \,].$ Complete the following reasoning to determine $inf(B)$ and $sup(B).$
The infimum of $B$ is the {{field-1}} of $B,$ and the supremum is the {{field-2}} of $B.$

Since $B$ is {{field-3}}, we have $inf(B)$ {{field-4}}.

Since $B$ is {{field-5}}, we have $sup(B)$ {{field-6}}.
worked_solution:
The infimum of $B$ is the greatest lower bound of $B,$ and the supremum is the smallest upper bound of $B.$

To find the infimum of this set, we must find the set containing **all** lower bounds of $B$ (i.e., the set of lower bounds) and take the maximum of this set.

Since $B$ is unbounded below, $B$ has no lower bounds, and $inf(B)=-\infty .$

Next, to find the supremum of this set, we must find the set containing **all** upper bounds of $B$ (i.e., the set of upper bounds) and take the minimum of this set.

In our case, we have the following:

- Any number in the set $x\ge \pi $ is greater than or equal to the elements of $B.$ Thus, the set $[\pi ,\infty )$ contains only upper bounds of $B.$

- Any number in the set $x<\pi $ is **not** an upper bound of $B.$ In other words, we can always find an element of $B$ that is greater than $x$ for any $x<\pi .$

Therefore, $[\pi ,\infty )$ is the set of upper bounds of $B,$ and

$$
sup(B)=min\,[\pi ,\infty )=\pi .
$$

The completed reasoning is given below.

The infimum of a set $B$ is the $\text{greatest lower bound}$ of $B,$ and the supremum is the $\text{smallest upper bound}$ of $B.$

Since $B$ is $\text{unbounded below},$ we have $inf(B)=-\infty .$

Since $B$ is $\text{bounded above},$ we have $sup(B)=\pi .$
